record.paper_title: Quantum Information Theory: Results and Open Problems
record.original_question: Suppose an ensemble consists of exactly two quantum states and one wants to maximize the accessible classical information obtained by measuring the received state. Must every measurement that attains this optimum be a von Neumann measurement, or can a more general positive-operator-valued measurement be strictly better even in the two-state case?

evidence.quote: If there are only two states in an ensemble, it has been conjectured that the measurement optimizing accessible information is always a von Neumann measurement, mainly because extensive computer experiments have not found a counterexample [11].
This conjecture has been proven for quantum states in two dimensions [22]. Our next example shows that this conjecture does not hold for ensembles composed of three or more states.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\{\rho_1,\rho_2\}$ be an ensemble of two quantum states on a finite-dimensional Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}$, with prior probabilities $p_1,p_2 \ge 0$ summing to $1$. A general measurement is described by a positive-operator-valued measure (POVM) $\{E_y\}_{y \in Y}$ on $\mathcal{H}$, i.e. a finite collection of positive semidefinite operators with $\sum_y E_y = I$. Given the ensemble and the POVM, the outcome $Y$ has conditional distribution $P(Y=y \mid X=i) = \mathrm{tr}(\rho_i E_y)$ for $i \in \{1,2\}$, and the accessible (mutual) information is
$$ I_{\mathrm{acc}}(\{p_i,\rho_i\}) \;=\; \sup_{\{E_y\}} I(X;Y), $$
where the supremum is over all POVMs. A von Neumann (projective) measurement is a POVM whose elements are mutually orthogonal projectors summing to $I$.

Question: For every two-state ensemble $\{(p_1,\rho_1),(p_2,\rho_2)\}$ on an arbitrary finite-dimensional Hilbert space, is the supremum defining $I_{\mathrm{acc}}$ attained by some von Neumann measurement? Equivalently, can no genuine (non-projective) POVM strictly exceed the best projective measurement when the ensemble contains only two states?
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture is proved for two states on a qubit (two-dimensional Hilbert space) by Keil, but in general dimension it remains open. A 2025 preprint refers to it as a longstanding open conjecture (sometimes called Shor's conjecture on quantum dichotomies) and makes progress on characterizing extremal optimizing measurements, but does not resolve the general case.

status_evidence.title: On Shor's conjecture on the accessible information of quantum dichotomies
status_evidence.snippet: Keil proved Shor's conjecture specifically for qubit dichotomies, but his proof is non-constructive... the optimal (von Neumann) measurement for any given qubit dichotomy remains given as the implicit solution of a transcendental equation.
status_evidence.claim: The general two-state conjecture remains open; only the qubit case is settled.

status_evidence.title: Proof of the orthogonal measurement conjecture for qubit states
status_evidence.snippet: Proof of the orthogonal measurement conjecture for qubit states
status_evidence.claim: The two-state conjecture is established in dimension two.
